content: If someone experiences severe symptoms such as losing consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. For other cases, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, it is essential to undergo laboratory and/or medical tests, such as an electrocardiogram (EKG), to monitor your condition. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember, unless it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in August 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Before taking ondansetron, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Ondansetron may lead to a condition affecting heart rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also heighten this risk, especially if you are using certain drugs like diuretics (water pills) or experiencing conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may pose risks to an unborn baby. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Consult your healthcare provider before breastfeeding. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. The risk of serotonin syndrome or toxicity increases if you are also taking other drugs that elevate serotonin levels. Examples include street drugs like MDMA (ecstasy), St. John’s wort, and certain antidepressants such as SSRIs (e.g., fluoxetine, paroxetine) or SNRIs (e.g., duloxetine, venlafaxine). If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away.
